not_exported.detail: Fleet's built-in skills (presentation-builder, svg-builder, mermaid-diagram-builder, generate-skill, fleet-guide and others) ship with Fleet's runtime. The exported agent doesn't have them.

left_behind: Conversations: past threads stay in Fleet. The deployment starts with none.
Sharing: people you shared the agent with in Fleet don't get access to the deployment.
Traces: the deployment traces to a new LangSmith project. Past traces stay in the Fleet agent's project.

connections.summary: The sandbox signs in to api.linear.app with an account the agent owns. An agent-owned connection can only be created after the deployment exists, so the rules that use it are commented out in `sandbox/__init__.py`.
steps: Register an OAuth app with the service the workspace's `linear` connection signs in to.

Create the connection. It prints the redirect URI to add to your app: `mda connections create linear-agent --authorize-url <authorization URL> --token-url <token URL> --client-id <client id> --secret-from-env LINEAR_AGENT_CLIENT_SECRET --authorize`. If `mda connections catalog` lists the service, pass `--oauth <service>` instead of `--authorize-url` and `--token-url`.
In `sandbox/__init__.py`, uncomment the rules that use `linear-agent`.

connections.summary: The sandbox signs in to www.googleapis.com with an account the agent owns. An agent-owned connection can only be created after the deployment exists, so the rules that use it are commented out in `sandbox/__init__.py`.
steps: Create the connection. It prints the redirect URI to add to your app: `mda connections create google --oauth google --client-id <client id> --secret-from-env GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET --scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly --authorize`.
In `sandbox/__init__.py`, uncomment the rules that use `google`.

sandbox: Copied Fleet's sandbox environment variables into `.env` as `SANDBOX_ENV_OPENAI_API_KEY`. `mda deploy` sends them to the deployment as secrets, and `sandbox/__init__.py` passes each to the sandbox under its Fleet name.
memory: `memory.py` gives the agent its own memory in `memories/agent/`. It starts empty, and the agent adds to it as it learns.
